messages:

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>

Subject: AcmeHealth  Private/VPC deployment post-call recap

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks for taking the time today  good conversation. Below is a short recap from our discovery + the proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points and goals (as we heard them):
- Regulatory/data residency: AcmeHealth needs all PHI-handling inference to remain in a US-only region, with evidence for audits.
- Network restrictions: Strict egress policy; incoming connections are tightly controlled. Preference for VPC peering or PrivateLink-style private connectivity; minimal public endpoints.
- Air-gap readiness: Long-term requirement to support an on-prem/air-gapped bundle for certain clinics and legacy environments.
- Control & key management: Customer-managed KMS/HSM for encryption keys and audit logs accessible for compliance reviews.
- Performance requirements: 99th percentile latency targets around 150-200ms for inference on small payloads; predictable throughput during batch runs.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Redwood Private: private control plane with VPC options + on-prem installers for air-gapped deployments.
- KMS integrations and audit log options; SOC 2 Type II report available (attached).
- Flexible networking: VPC peering or private endpoints; we can provide a pre-deploy checklist for firewall/NAT rules.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) Marissa: share the VPC architecture draft + SOC 2 summary (attached).
2) AcmeHealth: send network contact and a short list of required outbound IPs and egress constraints.
3) Dev: schedule technical deep-dive to walk through ports, NAT, and the air-gap approach (30-45m).
4) Both: draft a mutual action plan (MAP) and pilot timeline - target a small pilot in a single US region.

Attachments included: redwood-vpc-architecture-draft.png, redwood-soc2-type2.pdf

Proposed times for tech deep-dive:
- Thu 3/26 10:00-10:45 PT
- Thu 3/26 14:00-14:45 PT
- Fri 3/27 09:00-09:45 PT

If any of those work, I can send a calendar invite.

Thanks again - I’ll loop Dev in on the tech follow-up.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa  this is great and aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and asks from our security/networking side: 

1) Connectivity preferences: we generally prefer VPC peering where possible, but for cross-account access we sometimes use AWS PrivateLink. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports both models and whether there are any feature differences (e.g., metrics/tracing availability) across them?

2) Egress requirements: our environment allows only outbound HTTPS to a short list of FQDNs/IPs. We need the exact outbound endpoints (FQDN/IP ranges) that a Private deployment would need to reach, or confirmation if an entirely air-gapped installer would avoid outbound egress.

3) Data residency: pilot must be hosted in us-east-1. For the longer-term on-prem option, we will need an installation package that can operate completely offline (no outbound internet) and a process for KMS integration via local HSM. Is that an option and what team would own that work at Redwood?

4) Compliance artifacts: can you share the SOC 2 Type II report and a short checklist mapping Redwood capabilities to our HITRUST/HIPAA control requirements?

We can confirm the tech deep-dive on Thu 3/26 10:00 PT - please send an invite and include our network engineer (Bob Lee).

Appreciate the quick turnaround here.

Best,

Alice Johnson
Director, Security & Compliance
AcmeHealth

Quick answers to your bullets so Dev can expand during the call:
- VPC peering vs PrivateLink: we support both. PrivateLink can simplify cross-account access at the expense of some observability detail in the control plane; we can scope which metrics are available over each connection during the tech call.
- Egress endpoints: for Redwood Private with VPC peering, most data plane traffic stays within the peered VPCs. Control-plane calls (e.g., billing/console) may need outbound HTTPS unless you opt for our private control plane variant. I’ve attached a draft pre-deploy checklist that lists the minimal outbound endpoints; Dev will confirm exact IP ranges in the call.
- Air-gapped installer: yes - we have an on-prem bundle that can be installed offline; it requires a short initial handshake (for license activation) that we can do via an offline license token if needed. HSM/KMS integrations are supported; our Security Engineering team will own the integration work.

Attachments: private-deploy-precheck.md (short checklist)

Hi Alice / Bob - thanks for confirming the 10:00 PT slot and for the clear asks. A few technical notes I’ll walk through in the deep-dive:

- VPC models: both VPC peering and PrivateLink are supported. VPC peering maintains full network transparency (we can flow logs back to your monitoring) but requires route table and CIDR planning. PrivateLink uses ENIs and scales well for cross-account access; some control-plane-only telemetry may be proxied.

- Ports & protocols: primary data plane uses outbound TLS (443) from your instances to the model runtime when using our managed nodes; if you host the runtime on-prem, data plane stays within your network. Management/control plane can be scoped to our private control plane endpoints. We’ll enumerate exact FQDNs and IP ranges during the call and follow up with a CIDR-friendly list.

- Air-gap/on-prem: our offline bundle includes installers, configuration manifests, and an offline license token workflow. HSM integration is supported via PKCS#11 or KMIP - we’ll need your HSM provider + contact to validate.

- Audit & logs: we can provide structured audit logs (S3 or syslog export) and coordinate retention policies to satisfy your compliance team.

Prep for the call: please have a network engineer available (Bob suggested he can join) and, if possible, a sample of the egress rules you currently enforce so I can point to specific exceptions we may request.

Attaching: private-deploy-precheck.md (checklist)

Thanks - see you at 10:00 PT.

Dev Patel
